text: While gradient checkpointing curbs activation growth, it incurs ≈30% recomputation overhead.

label: specific
text: Moreover, on-the-fly dequantization in QLoRA lowers token throughput compared to 16-bit LoRA when memory headroom suffices.

label: specific
text: To evaluate these methods without conflating activations with adapter overhead, we specify a controlled benchmark on a 24 GB GPU (NVIDIA RTX 4090 or A10G) adapting LLaMA-3-8B on Alpaca (52k samples).

label: specific
text: The primary baseline is 16-bit LoRA (r=16, =32 across all linear projections), evaluated alongside DoRA (detached norm), QLoRA (NF4 base), LoftQ (4-bit initialized), QA-LoRA (INT4 group-wise), and an out-of-memory full fine-tuning reference.

label: specific
text: Controls: Random seeds are fixed to 42 across Python, NumPy, and PyTorch CUDA (torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True).

label: specific
text: We fix micro-batch size to B = 2, gradient accumulation to 8 (effective batch 16), gradient checkpointing enabled, AdamW (lr = 2 × 10-4), and contexts L \1024, 2048\.

label: specific
text: Additionally, QLoRA's throughput penalty during training dequantization and QA-LoRA's reliance on custom quantized kernels represent practical trade-offs rarely captured by parameter counts alone.
